fact: Lands Minister of State Harriet Ntabazi said the ministry's survey, mapping and registration departments have been equipped with upgraded digital systems, a blockchain-based land records system has been developed, and satellite and drones will be used to capture parcels.
Minister Ntabazi said that with the new digitalisation system applicants enter their data in the computer at district level and have their title printed.

The Uganda Land Commission is preparing a nationwide GIS-based digital registry of all government-owned land, with ministries asked to submit records and city and municipal authorities verifying boundaries.

fact: The Minister of Lands, Housing and Urban Development, Judith Nabakooba, described the Uganda National Land Information System (UGNLIS) as a public portal where citizens can check land status, confirm ownership and track transactions.

The Minister said citizens can check land status and confirm ownership on the UGNLIS public portal, and the author urged landowners to check land interests through digitalised land services before transactions.
